migration.description: Add immutable approval revision history beside the stable-ID current CAS projection and provide a versioned Run-bound keyset position.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one execution-domain candidate following migration 00011; this migration is reserved for the Server-side approval revision-history write and read boundary.

compatibility_assessment.reason: Public approval IDs, response fields, limits, authorization and exact resolution CAS remain stable, while the opaque cursor gains an internal version and the additive history table makes newly written same-ID revisions unreadable as complete history to projection-only older writers/readers.

durable_state.description: The current approval projection remains the exact write-side CAS row keyed by stable native request ID. Immutable history rows are keyed by (id, revision), retain raw context and requested-event identity, and remain readable across old execution generations.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL table and keyset indexes managed by the embedded Goose migration history. Existing execution_approvals rows are copied only as one provable snapshot at their current persisted revision.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Phase-one approval-history candidate containing migrations 00009 through 00011.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one stable-ID approval revision-history candidate containing migration 00012.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Older projection-only writers/readers may participate only in the pre-cutover drain window. They must be fenced before any new revision is written; after that point switchback requires a history-capable candidate.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create execution_approval_revisions with stable approval ID plus revision primary key, raw context/event linkage, state and resolution identity columns.
Create the Run-bound cursor index and requested-event lookup index after the backfill so a failure proves the complete table and backfill unit rolls back.

dml_changes.description: Copy exactly one history row from each current execution_approvals row at its persisted (id, revision), preserving raw context, requested_event_id, status and timestamps. Missing older revisions are not synthesized.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati: No discarded approval revision is reconstructed.
A current projection row without a matching history snapshot after migration is a failed migration/compatibility state, not an empty history result.

progress_signals: A fresh PostgreSQL schema is migrated through 00011 with a real current approval row, then 00012 backfills exactly one matching history row and records migration 00012 only after the full Goose transaction commits.

A deliberate 00012 index-name collision fails after table creation and backfill, leaves version 12 unapplied and leaves no partial history table or rows; removing only the collision permits forward re-entry.
A repeated database migration leaves exactly one history table, one primary key, both named indexes and one applied 00012 history record.
The new writer checks projection/history agreement before serving history reads or writing revision state, and old projection-only state drift fails closed instead of silently losing a page.
pause_points: Before applying 00012, verify the candidate source identity, the 00011 schema and PostgreSQL migration lock availability.
After 00012 commits, verify one history row for every current projection row at its current (id, revision) before admitting new approval revision writes.
Drain and fence all projection-only writers before accepting the first post-migration higher-revision approval request.
If a projection/history guard fails, stop approval history traffic and repair forward; do not switch back to an older writer after new revision history exists.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version or a corrected re-entry after a rolled-back 00012 transaction; do not invent missing revisions or rewrite raw history

required_test_evidence: The PostgreSQL path from 00011 to 00012 backfills a current approval row exactly once, retains raw context and requested_event_id and leaves the current projection unchanged.

A deliberate 00012 index collision rolls back table creation and the backfill, leaves migration 00012 unapplied, and the same migration re-enters successfully after only the deliberate collision is removed.
Repeated migration discovery leaves one history table, the Run cursor index, requested-event index and applied migration record.

Same stable approval ID with revisions written at equal created_at values returns every revision through version-2 cursors without skips; current resolution changes only the matching history revision.
A legacy cursor is accepted only for a unique persisted (run_id, created_at, id) position and ambiguous, missing, malformed or cross-run positions fail closed.
A current projection with missing or divergent history is rejected by the read/write guard, and old projection-only writers are excluded from the post-cutover acceptance window.
